title: Colimit of quotient Hom complexes is the torsion subcomplex
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $J$ an ideal and $K$ a nonnegative cochain complex of $R$-modules. For each $n\in\mathbf N$ take the complex $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/J^n,K)$ as in [lem-sbc-ext-injective-resolution-comparison], with transition maps given by precomposition with $R/J^{n+1}\to R/J^n$. Its filtered colimit is isomorphic as a cochain complex to $\Gamma_J(K)$, where $\Gamma_J$ is applied termwise and is the ideal-power torsion functor [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor]. No finite-generation hypothesis is required.

proof.text: For each n and module N, evaluation at 1 sends a map R/J^n → N to an element killed by J^n and hence to Ideal.primaryComponent N J. If evaluations of two maps agree, write any quotient element as a scalar multiple of 1 to prove that the maps agree. For a torsion element x choose an exponent n that kills it and factor the explicit scalar map a ↦ a • x through the quotient by J^n, using Submodule.liftQ. Its evaluation is x. Evaluation commutes with all quotient transitions. Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf′ therefore proves that the underlying-type cocone is colimiting. Reflect this colimit through the module forgetful functor (shrinking its filtered-colimit reflection to universe zero).

Apply these evaluation maps in every degree of K. They commute with the differential because both composites send f to d(f(1)). They also commute with quotient transitions, so form a cocone of complexes with vertex the termwise torsion complex. Its evaluation in every degree is the preceding colimit cocone. HomologicalComplex.isColimitOfEval proves that the complex cocone is colimiting. The uniqueness of colimits gives the displayed complex isomorphism. The explicit Hom complex construction is homComplexDiagram of lem-sbc-ext-injective-resolution-comparison; its comparison theorem is not used in this algebraic proof.

theorem nonempty_colimit_quotientHomComplex_iso_torsion
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (J : Ideal R)
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℕ) :
    Nonempty (colimit
      ((localCohomology.ringModIdeals (localCohomology.idealPowersDiagram J)).op ⋙
        homComplexDiagram K) ≅
      ((idealPowerTorsion J).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj K)
